podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Gig on Elvis' Birthday (January 8, 1989)
podcast.body: Dread Zeppelin's very first gig took place on January 8th, 1989, which would have been the real Elvis Presley's 54th birthday. The concept admittedly started as a joke. "Their first gig, January 8th, 1989, on what would have been the real Elvis' 54th birthday. And yes, everybody will admit that this started as a joke."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Collaboration with Dave Stewart (1990)
podcast.body: By the end of 1990, Dread Zeppelin had recorded a significant amount of material with Dave Stewart, known from the Eurythmics. "and by the end of 1990, they'd recorded a bunch of stuff with Dave Stewart, the guy from the Eurythmics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Expanded Repertoire
podcast.body: The band eventually broadened its repertoire beyond just Led Zeppelin songs to include material from The Yardbirds, another band associated with Jimmy Page, and Bob Marley, which made sense given their reggae style. "But Dread Zeppelin eventually expanded their repertoire to include the Yard Birds, another Jimmy Page band, and Bob Marley, which made sense, I guess."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Ironical "Free Bird" Performance
podcast.body: Dread Zeppelin is noted for playing along with the "Free Bird" meme by performing the song in their own fashion when requested by the audience during their sets. "Like these guys, Dread Zeppelin, if you call for free bird during one of their sets, they oblige in this fashion."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Longevity (25+ Years)
podcast.body: Dread Zeppelin is still together today and continues to play gigs more than 25 years after their formation, demonstrating their enduring appeal. "Now the group is still together today, they're still playing gigs more than 25 years later."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Original Material Development
podcast.body: The band also began recording their own original material, moving beyond strictly covers. "and they also started recording original material."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pasadena Origin (Evolved from The Prime Movers)
podcast.body: The band originated in Pasadena, California, evolving out of a previous group known as The Prime Movers. "Dread Zeppelin came together in Pasadena, California, evolving out of a group called The Prime Movers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reggae Led Zeppelin Covers
podcast.body: Dread Zeppelin's core concept was playing reggae covers of Led Zeppelin songs, a pursuit they took seriously despite initial perceptions as a novelty act. "They were pretty serious about what they were doing, which was playing reggae covers of Led Zeppelin songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Serious Business Development
podcast.body: As they played more, people began to take them more seriously, transforming their initial "fun" concept into a legitimate business. "The more they played, the more people took them seriously. Not too seriously, though. Everybody understood that it was about having fun, but this fun turned into a business, a real business."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Signed to IRS Records
podcast.body: Dread Zeppelin signed with IRS Records, which was R.E.M.'s former label. "They were then signed to IRS Records, REM's old label."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Stewart Adamson's Fandom
podcast.body: Stewart Adamson of Big Country was a significant fan of Dread Zeppelin. "Steward Adamson, a big country, remember them? He was a big fan of these guys."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tortelvis - Elvis Impersonator Frontman
podcast.body: After The Prime Movers imploded, the remaining members reformed with an Elvis impersonator named Tortelvis, whose real name was Greg Tortelli. At the time he joined, he weighed nearly 300 pounds. "When that group imploded, they started up again, this time with an Elvis impersonator who went by the name Tort Elvis out front. His real name was Greg Tortelli, and at the time he joined the band, he was pushing 300 pounds."
